LESSON: POPULATION STRUCTURE - KENYA - GERMANY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and relationships
Topic 3.4: Population Structure - Kenya - Germany
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Population Structure - Kenya - Germany, part of People, Population and relationships in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is population structure of a country important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms and concepts related to population structure,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify sources of population data in a country,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain factors determining population structure in Kenya and Germany,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. construct age-sex population pyramids of developed and developing countries,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. determine the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate the differences between developed and developing countries for sustainable development. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Population Structure - Kenya - Germany in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign terms and concepts related to population structure,

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify sources of population data in a country,

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain factors determining population structure in Kenya and Germany,

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. construct age-sex population pyramids of developed and developing countries,

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. determine the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a society,

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. appreciate the differences between developed and developing countries for sustainable development. ●

   Population Structure - Kenya - Germany helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Population Structure - Kenya - Germany together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: Learners undertake the task of drawing and displaying age-sex population pyramid of developed and

developing countries (Germany and Kenya),

● Communication and collaboration: Learners work collaboratively as they discuss the significance of population structure in distribution

of national resources in a society.

Values:
● Unity: learners collaborate with others as they brainstorm in groups, sources of population data (Kenya and Germany) and make notes

and present.

● Respect: learners appreciate diverse opinion as they brainstorm in groups, sources of population data (Kenya and Germany) make notes

and present.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Citizenship: Learners acquire knowledge on population structure of Kenya and Germany together with its influence on distribution of

resources in society.

● Effective Communication: Learners engage a resource person as they discuss factors determining population structure in Kenya and

Germany.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners employ mathematics knowledge to draw and display in class population structure of Kenya and Germany.

Learners communicate effectively as they discuss in groups the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a

society helping them develop language skills in English, Kiswahili, and Kenyan Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resource:

digital resources, resource person, print resources, government census reports,

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. sign terms and concepts related to population structure,
2. identify sources of population data in a country,
3. explain factors determining population structure in Kenya and Germany,
4. construct age-sex population pyramids of developed and developing countries,
5. determine the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a society,
6. appreciate the differences between developed and developing countries for sustainable development. ●

Remember the key question: Why is population structure of a country important?
